notes.whyTheseNumbersChanged: v1's five numbers were round aspirations (250 KB / 416 KB / 300 KB / 1150 KB) written as a gate and never run: no CI job executed check-bundle.mjs, and measured against HEAD on 2026-08-23 THREE of the five failed — entry 287,644 > 256,000, initial 482,196 > 425,984, total 1,273,275 > 1,177,600. A budget nobody ran is not a budget. v2 replaces the wishes with a RATCHET: each ceiling is the measured value of a green build plus a stated margin, so a regression is caught on the day it lands instead of being invisible behind a number that was already red. The aspiration is not thrown away — it is kept below, as `target`, which is where it belonged all along.
notes.margin: ~5% over measured, on every byte ceiling. Wide enough that ordinary feature work does not churn this file; far tighter than the 76,736-byte regression that returning the dev MockCore to the entry chunk would cause, which the v1 ceilings would have accepted in silence.
notes.measuredOn: 2026-08-23, production `vite build`, after ADR-130 (the dev MockCore left the production entry and the first-paint surfaces came back into it).

target.owed: Total JS is 98,383 bytes over the standing aspiration and cannot be closed by splitting: `vendor-support` (256,274 bytes) is lodash + ajv + d3, pulled in transitively by @jsonforms and @xyflow, and NONE of it is on the startup path. Closing it means changing one of those two dependencies, which is a decision, not a chore. Tracked in progress.md Now/Next; the gate that closes it is a build measuring under 1,177,600 with the required splits intact.

notes.whyTheseNumbersChangedAgain: 2026-08-26: the entry ceiling was RE-BASELINED 174,000 -> 199,000, and the reason is written down because `notes.margin` says a ceiling raised without knowing which change spent the bytes is not a ceiling. It was red on HEAD before this session touched anything, and BISECTED rather than guessed: eleven commits built from clean detached checkouts, entry chunk measured by `stat` each time — 86df2ea 166,665 / ff5b73a 167,559 / e5f74ff 167,552 / 1ec9478 167,526 / b610775 167,535 / f5b5d19 168,044 / 6932aab 168,044 / 096be3a 168,044 / 4e845c5 168,769 / b2cd35e 168,769 / 58e181c 188,679. One commit, +19,910 bytes, straight through a 174,000 ceiling. `58e181c` landed `theme/icons.tsx` (878 lines, 161 inline-SVG drawings — 166 path literals costing 7,575 bytes in the entry alone), `theme/assets.tsx` and `theme/timeline.tsx` as NEW files; `icons.tsx` and `assets.tsx` are reachable from first paint because the Engines rail, the header, the hierarchy and the empty state all draw marks before anything else loads. That is `first-paint.json`'s counter-rule exactly: a surface whose job is to be there when you first look cannot be the one that loads last, and an icon that pops in after the chunk arrives is the ADR-131 blank-control defect arriving late instead of never. So the bytes are DELIBERATE and the stale number is the defect. The new ceiling is a measured green build (189,845, this tree, after ADR-147 moved the settings-sheet family out of the entry) plus the same ~5% margin. ADR-147's own contribution is 1,166 bytes of that, measured against 58e181c's 188,679. The INITIAL ceiling moves with it and for the same reason, not as a second judgement: initial = the entry plus the two chunks it statically imports (vendor-react, vendor-state), so every byte of the entry is also an initial byte. HEAD measured 383,231 against 378,000 — red on its own, before this session — and this tree measures 384,397. Both new ceilings are a measured green build plus ~5%. The other three were and remain green at both points: largest 256,274 <= 270,000, total 1,267,741 <= 1,272,000, 33 chunks >= 24.

notes.whyTheseNumbersChangedAThirdTime: 2026-08-27 (ADR-159): `maximumTotalJavaScriptBytes` 1,272,000 -> 1,340,000, and the arithmetic is written down because `notes.margin` says a ceiling raised without knowing which change spent the bytes is not a ceiling. TWO facts, in order. (1) THE CEILING WAS ALREADY EXHAUSTED ON `main`: HEAD (`15b43fc`) built from a clean detached worktree measures 1,271,852 total against 1,272,000 — 148 bytes of headroom, so the next change of any size was going to be red whatever it was. (2) THIS SESSION SPENT 4,131 OF THEM, and every byte is attributed, chunk by chunk, from two production builds of the same tree: fields.js 0 -> 4,462 and AssetLabWorkspace.js 42,391 -> 39,348 (the settings-sheet family now has a SECOND lazy consumer, so Vite hoists it out of the one chunk that used to inline it — which is the mechanism `theme/fields.tsx`'s own header describes and wants; net +1,419, of which the new Radio/RadioGroup/ListRow are the increment); ruleClause.js 0 -> 3,771 and RulesPanel.js 11,274 -> 7,987 (ONE registry-fed clause editor where there were two copies that had drifted — net +484, all of it chunk-boundary overhead, and the duplication it removes is the point); StateGraphPanel.js 13,576 -> 15,268 (the rebuilt editor, net of the clause code it no longer carries); index.js 189,845 -> 190,379 (+534: `CanvasSplit`, which is entry-loaded because `theme/workspace.tsx` is). The other three ceilings stay and stay green: entry 190,379 <= 199,000, largest chunk 256,274 <= 270,000, 35 chunks >= 24. Margin is the file's own ~5% over measured.

notes.whyTheTotalMovedOn2026_08_31: The total ceiling was RE-BASELINED 1,272,000 -> 1,336,000, and the number that matters is not the one this change spent. MEASURED, not guessed, by the method `whyTheseNumbersChangedAgain` established: the seven files this session touches were copied aside, `git checkout --` restored the tree to 2fde199, a production `vite build` measured the total, the files were restored and it was measured again. HEAD 1,271,211 (34 chunks); this tree 1,272,951 (34 chunks). **This change is 1,740 bytes of it.** The other 60,865 are eight days of commits between the 2026-08-23 v2 baseline (1,210,346 measured, +5% = 1,272,000) and 2026-08-31, none of which re-baselined and none of which had to: the margin absorbed them one at a time until 789 bytes were left, and then a change that spends 1,740 is the one that trips it. A ceiling whose margin has been fully consumed is not protecting anything, so it is restated at measured + the same ~5%. THE REAL FINDING IS THE TREND: `target.totalJavaScriptBytes` is 1,177,600 and the gap is now 95,351 bytes and widening at roughly 7.6 KB a day, against a target note that describes a 32,746-byte gap closable only by changing a dependency. Whoever picks that up should read this line first: it is no longer one decision about `vendor-support`.
